events.title: Texas Declaration of Independence
events.description: Delegates meeting at Washington-on-the-Brazos formally adopted the Texas Declaration of Independence, announcing separation from Mexico and the creation of the Republic of Texas.
events.significance: It established the independent Republic of Texas, which existed until its annexation by the United States in 1845 and set the stage for the Mexican-American War.

events.title: Rutherford B. Hayes Declared Winner of the 1876 Presidential Election
events.description: Congress declared Rutherford B. Hayes the winner of the disputed 1876 presidential election over Samuel Tilden, just days before the inauguration, after the Electoral Commission awarded him all contested electoral votes.
events.significance: The outcome was tied to the Compromise of 1877, which led to the withdrawal of federal troops from the South and effectively ended Reconstruction.

events.title: Birth of Mikhail Gorbachev
events.description: Mikhail Gorbachev was born in Privolnoye, in the Stavropol region of the Soviet Union. He rose through the Communist Party to become General Secretary in 1985 and later the last leader of the USSR.
events.significance: His policies of glasnost and perestroika, along with arms control agreements with the West, helped end the Cold War and led to the dissolution of the Soviet Union in 1991. He won the Nobel Peace Prize in 1990.

events.title: Wilt Chamberlain Scores 100 Points
events.description: Playing for the Philadelphia Warriors against the New York Knicks in Hershey, Pennsylvania, Wilt Chamberlain scored 100 points in a single NBA game, with the Warriors winning 169-147.
events.significance: It remains the highest individual scoring performance in NBA history and one of the most famous records in professional sports.

events.title: First Test Flight of the Concorde
events.description: The Concorde supersonic passenger airliner, developed jointly by Britain and France, made its first test flight from Toulouse, France.
events.significance: Concorde became the first successful supersonic commercial airliner, entering service in 1976 and flying transatlantic routes at over twice the speed of sound until its retirement in 2003.
